subject: Follow-up: privacy routing, DPA options & SCC selection for Fintegrity
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintegrity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: privacy routing, DPA options & SCC selection for Fintegrity

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Call highlights
- Use case: Fintegrity will use Redwood Inference to power anonymized transaction summarization for EU customers (no PHI).
- Hosting requirement: primary tenancy in eu-west with option to pin to EU-only nodes.
- Compliance asks: SOC 2 Type II report, DPA with SCCs, and a short vendor security questionnaire (VSQ).

Questions we have for you (single-threaded):
1) Controller/processor mapping: on the call you indicated Fintegrity would be the controller for end-customer PII and Redwood would act as processor. Can you confirm that is the right mapping for this integration?
2) SCC preference: do you require the EU Standard Contractual Clauses for controller-to-processor transfers (commonly \"Module 2\" / controller-to-processor), or do you need a controller-to-controller setup?
3) SOC 2: will a SOC 2 Type II report (latest 12 months) suffice, or do you need additional attestation or supplementary evidence (pen tests, infra diagrams)?

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- I’ll share our DPA options and a short mapping doc explaining SCC variants we support (attached: redwood-dpa-options-summary.pdf).
- If you confirm controller=Fintegrity / processor=Redwood, Marissa will kick off our DPA drafting and legal will prepare the proper SCC annex.
- We’ll open the formal VSQ in our portal (I’ll send the link) — this typically takes 1–2 business days to populate.

Would appreciate confirmation on Q1–Q2 so we can lock the right DPA path. If you prefer, we can prepare both variants (controller-to-processor and controller-to-controller) and you can pick one in the procurement review.

Thanks — I’ll stay on this and loop legal once you confirm.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: redwood-dpa-options-summary.pdf, rdw-security-briefing-2026.pdf
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintegrity.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: privacy routing, DPA options & SCC selection for Fintegrity

Diego —

Great recap, thanks. Short answers below: 

1) Controller/processor: confirmed — Fintegrity is controller for the transaction data we collect from our customers; Redwood will be a processor for any data processed on our behalf.
2) SCC preference: procurement/legal generally asks for the controller-to-processor SCC set. We typically request the standard Clauses for controller-to-processor transfers; providing the controller-to-controller variant will slow review. So please prioritize the controller->processor SCC mapping.
3) SOC 2: a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the last 12 months is fine. We may request your SOC auditor contact for validation if needed.

A couple of notes: 
- We will need the DPA in a fairly standard DPA + SCC Annex layout, and procurement will run redlines.
- On hosting: we prefer EU-only hosting for production; dev/test can be multiregion.

Please go ahead and share the DPA draft and the VSQ link. I’ll loop our procurement mailbox (procurement@fintegrity.com) for redlines.

Thanks — Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform Security | Fintegrity
olivia.chen@fintegrity.com
